title: Cue Ensemble Stitchbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchbook for assembling small reusable "cues" (instruction fragments) and stitching them into few-shot ensembles. Goal: build compact, robust templates that degrade gracefully across model variants and expose where brittleness comes from. Not a finished library — more of an ideation+repro log.

High-level approach notes:
- Think of cues as composable micro-instructions (intent-cue, format-cue, constraint-cue, example-cue).
- Keep examples minimal: 2–4 shots per micro-domain. Avoid overfitting to toy phrasing.
- Focus on failure modes explicitly: hallucination, instruction-ignoring, repetition, early-stop.
- Aim for templates that are robust with temperature 0.0–0.6 and both causal and chat-style APIs.

Quick templates (working drafts):
1) Intent+Anchor (compact):
   - Instruction: "You are an assistant that answers succinctly and cites the reason in 1 sentence."
   - Anchor: "If unsure, say 'insufficient info' rather than guessing."
   - Example-cue: 2-shot pairs with question -> terse answer + reasoning.
   - Use-case: FAQs, UI tooltip generation.

2) Multi-step scaffolding (for reasoning):
   - Instruction: "Break the task into numbered steps, then provide final answer."
   - Constraint-cue: "Each step <= 20 words."
   - Shots: 3 examples that show explicit chain-of-thought removed (model should not output internal chain unless asked).
   - Note: This reduces hallucination but increases token cost. Keep for critical outputs only.

3) Format-first (structured output):
   - Instruction: "Return JSON with keys: summary, evidence, confidence (0-1). No extra text."
   - Example-cue: 2 examples covering high-confidence and low-confidence cases.
   - Pitfall: models sometimes append trailing text; add explicit 'only JSON'.

Few-shot packs (short lists to swap in/out):
- Pack A: factual Q/A (2 shots): domain-general short-answer, one ambiguous question.
- Pack B: instruction-following (3 shots): focus on obeying constraints (length, format).
- Pack C: anti-hallucination (2 shots): show 'I don't know' followed by a safe alternative suggestion.

Observed failure cases (examples + quick repro):
- Failure: Overconfident hallucination on partially specified queries
  - Prompt excerpt: "Tell me the relationship between X and Y in 18th c. contexts."
  - Output: confidently invents a source/quote.
  - Quick mitigation tried: add anchor "Only reference facts you can assert as widely accepted. If unsure, say 'insufficient info'" — reduced hallucinations but made model prefer 'insufficient' too often in simple cases.

- Failure: Format drift — model adds commentary around required JSON
  - Repro: format-first template without a closing delimiter.
  - Fix that helped: wrap JSON in triple markers and add explicit penalty phrase "DO NOT add commentary". Still occasional drift on older model variants.

- Failure: Example entanglement — a single example's phrasing dominates style of answer across unrelated questions
  - Observation: overly-fluent example causes model to mimic style even when brevity requested.
  - Mitigation: diversify shots and include a negative example (show what not to do).

Experiment log (short entries):
- 2024-03-09: Tried intent+anchor with model v1-small, temp=0.2. Result: fewer hallucinations, but higher occurrence of 'I don't know' for borderline queries.
- 2024-04-01: Format-first with triple markers + 2-shot pack on v1-medium, temp=0.0. Clean JSON in 83% of prompts; remaining 17% had trailing comments.
- 2024-05-18: Added an explicit 'fallback suggestion' in anti-hallucination shot (e.g., propose a safe heuristic). Improved user value when model refuses.

Evaluation plan (light):
- Create a small eval set (~120 items): 40 factual, 40 ambiguous/insufficient, 40 formatting-focused.
- Metrics: exact-structure match (for JSON), hallucination rate (binary), helpfulness score (1-5 annotation).
- Baselines: nothing (zero-shot), single-template few-shot, ensemble of 3 cues.

Repro details (what I run locally/in console):
- Typical API call: chat endpoint with system role = intent-cue; user role contains examples (few-shot) + query; model param: temperature=0.0|0.3, max_tokens=300, top_p=0.95.
- Model tags used in tests: v1-small, v1-medium, v2-chat (internal naming).
- Note: include explicit 'stop' tokens when testing format-heavy outputs.

Open hypotheses to test next:
- H1: Splitting intent and format into system vs user roles reduces format drift compared to single-block prompts.
- H2: Adding a single negative example (what not to do) reduces example entanglement without adding confusion.
- H3: For ambiguous queries, giving a safe fallback heuristics line increases perceived helpfulness more than an outright refusal.

To-dos / quick tasks:
- [ ] Build eval harness for 120-item set (assign to Rafael).
- [ ] Try system-role split experiments (run across v1-medium and v2-chat).
- [ ] Add 5 negative-example shots to Pack B and re-evaluate.
- [ ] Draft a short one-pager on 'cue composability' for the prompt-lab readout.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep templates terse — long instruction blocks become brittle.
- When copying examples into shared library, normalize punctuation and remove author-specific idioms.
- Slack: #prompt-lab thread often helpful for quick sanity checks.

Relevant links and tickets:
- Linear: RED-1427 (build cue eval harness)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lab/pull/86 (initial cue serialization)
- Confluence stub: cue-lib-v1 (draft page)

End of scratchbook entry.

(If revisiting: try a tiny synthetic dataset that simulates underspecified user intents vs high-certainty facts — should make metric signal clearer.)
